data.title: The recently lost file upload feature in the Nextcloud app for Android
data.author: morsch
data.article_summary: Nextcloud团队解释了Android版Nextcloud应用中文件上传功能的问题。自2024年中期以来，Google撤销了一项关键权限，导致用户无法上传所有类型文件，只能上传照片和视频。尽管Nextcloud自2016年推出以来一直拥有该功能，且未收到安全问题的反馈，但Google仍拒绝恢复权限。这导致数百万用户受影响，只能上传媒体文件，无法上传其他文件。Nextcloud认为这是Google利用其平台所有者地位打压竞争对手的行为，类似于过去微软通过限制功能打压WordPerfect的做法。团队对用户 frustration 表示理解，但目前无法解决此问题。不过，在F-Droid等替代应用商店中，用户仍可使用无限制的版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google对独立开发者和小型开发商的权限限制以及其潜在的反竞争行为

不同观点：
• AmazingTurtle：认为Google打着“最小权限”的旗号，实际上为自己的第一方应用提供了特权访问，而独立开发商只能推出半成品的产品。这导致用户失去功能和选择，小型开发者浪费大量时间与政策机器人争论。
• moonshot5：从AOSP平台开发者的角度出发，认为Google Drive并没有给予特别待遇，且SAF（存储访问框架）可以满足Nextcloud的需求。同时指出过去*MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE*权限被广泛滥用。
• thombles：提到SyncThing Android应用因类似问题停止分发，目前只有非官方版本可用。
• jeroenhd：反驳Nextcloud关于SAF不适用于其需求的声明，认为SAF可以用于共享文件，但有些限制确实不适合Nextcloud。
• patcon：认为Google拒绝承担监督责任，通过锁定其他玩家来管理市场，是不恰当的。建议如果监督成本高，可以收取象征性费用。
• scottbez1：提供历史案例，指出Google曾为自己的应用设计专属API，而拒绝其他竞争者使用，显示出反竞争行为。
• inigoalonso：从欧盟数字市场法的角度出发，认为Google的行为是滥用平台权力，阻碍欧洲技术发展，必须通过法律制止。
• dzikimarian：用户体验角度，抱怨自己的设备限制访问数据，列举多个不便之处，表示不满。
• aborsy：认为Google可以提示用户给予权限，剩下的由用户决定。
• tuga2099：质疑Google Drive应用是否可以上传所有文件类型。
• jsnell：提供了一个相关讨论的链接，指向Hacker News上的讨论。
• igtztorrero：回顾Google的企业格言变化，认为其自2015年后变得像微软一样，具有反竞争倾向。
• BLenkomo：希望同时拥有完全文件访问和受控访问的选项，认为不是所有用户都想要Nextcloud的完全同步功能。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Google是否通过权限限制给予自己第一方应用特权，从而阻碍独立开发商和小型开发者竞争。
• 用户体验和数据访问的限制也引发了用户的不满，特别是在与其他平台（如iOS）比较时。
• 法律和监管（如欧盟的数字市场法）被认为是可能解决这一问题的途径。

43981170.article_content:
Unhappy with the recently lost file upload feature in the Nextcloud app for Android? So are we. Let us explain.
Post date
May 13, 2025
Categories
Business
News
Opinion
Author
Christoph Weissthaner
Facebook
X
LinkedIn
Mastodon
Dear users,
We are aware that for some months, Nextcloud file uploads for Android users have not been working as expected: you cannot upload all data to your Nextcloud, only photos and videos. We have seen your complaints in various forums such as the Nextcloud
help forum
, on
GitHub
,
Reddit
, or other
forums
.
As your experience with the Nextcloud Files app for Android has worsened, we wanted to share the background. Google has revoked a critical permission to sync all files. Despite multiple appeals since mid-2024, Google has refused to reinstate it, forcing us to limit file uploads for millions of users.
The Nextcloud file uploads issue means that some media files, such as pictures and videos, can still be uploaded from Android devices to Nextcloud, but all other files cannot. And that is pretty much beating the purpose.
Google is stating security concerns as a reason for revoking the permission. This is hard to believe for us. Nextcloud has had this feature since its inception in 2016, and we have never heard about any security concerns from Google about it. Moreover, several Big Tech apps as well as Google’s own still have this. What we think: Google owning the platform means they can and are giving themselves preferential treatment.
Despite multiple appeals since mid-2024, Google has refused to reinstate the permission, blocking automated Nextcloud file uploads for millions of users.
To make it crystal clear: All of you as users have a worse Nextcloud Files client because Google wanted that. We understand and share your frustration, but there is nothing we can do.
The more tech-savvy of you are certainly able to use the alternative app store, such as
F-Droid
. But for our user base of roughly one million users on the app store, this will hardly be an option.
For transparency, we have compiled more background below to help you understand the Nextcloud file upload issue and how Google is abusing its gatekeeper position.
Sincerely, the Nextcloud team
Error message “Changes to auto upload” from Nextcloud app for Android
What happened
with Nextcloud file uploads for Android?
The permission for read and write access
to all file types for the Nextcloud Files app for Android was granted in 2011. In September 2024, an update of the Nextcloud app for Android was refused out of the blue. We have been asked to remove the permission to all files or use “a more privacy aware replacement” like Storage Access Framework (SAF) or MediaStore API.
SAF cannot be used, as it is for sharing/exposing our files to other apps, so the reviewer clearly misunderstood our app workflow. MediaStore API cannot be used as it does not allow access to other files, but only media files.
Despite multiple appeals from our side and sharing additional background, Google is not considering reinstating uploads for all files. Instead of working collaboratively to solve the issue, we only receive the same copy-and-paste answers or links to documentation. With nearly a million users and an 8-year history, it is hard to argue that our Android app has no credibility. So it is very surprising to get treated this way to the disadvantage of our users.
As we needed to release bug fixes to our users and customers, and there was no other way to discuss, we chose to comply with Google’s new regulations. Google finally accepted our newest update, which limits uploads for our users.
The Android app itself still works with the permission, and we released new versions on the external F-Droid store. So the limit is a “purely” Google Play Store-related problem.
The bigger picture: Big Tech gatekeeping in action
This might look like a small technical detail, but it is clearly part of a pattern of actions to fight the competition. What we are experiencing is a piece of the script from the Big Tech playbook.
It is a clear example of Big Tech gatekeeping smaller software vendors, making the products of their competitors worse or unable to provide the same services as the giants themselves sell. As they own the platform, they can — and do — give themselves preferential treatment.
A famous example of this in the past was Microsoft, which blocked certain capabilities from Windows to ensure WordPerfect users had a worse experience than people who picked Microsoft Word. Today, Google creates rules in the name of security that make it hard to
build products that compete with them
.
We suppose Google can’t get away with this versus Apple or Microsoft, as those companies would retaliate. But smaller companies, especially those building disruptive technologies like ours, are fair game for them.
Big Tech is scared that small players like Nextcloud will disrupt them, like they once disrupted other companies. So they try to shut the door.
Then they have

data.title: VPN firm says it didn't know customers had lifetime subscriptions, cancels them
data.author: maxloh
data.article_summary: VPNSecure的新所有者取消了终身订阅服务，引发了用户的不满。新 owners 声称在收购VPNSecure时并不知情这些终身订阅，因此无法继续提供服务。自2023年收购以来，他们发现大量资源被终身订阅用户占用，导致服务压力增加。公司提供折扣订阅作为补偿，但用户普遍表示不满，认为公司在沟通和处理上缺乏透明度和同情心。用户在Trustpilot上大量留下差评，而VPNSecure则回应称，他们本可以选择关闭服务，但选择了更艰难的道路，并强调不会再出售终身订阅。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VPNSecure收购后的责任承担及相关商业模式的可持续性

不同观点：
• [cookiengineer] 认为VPNSecure在收购声明中提到只收购技术、域名和客户数据库，但不包括责任，这种做法存在法律问题。他以购买毒品后不对警察承认责任为例，质疑为何这种行为未被立即起诉，暗示这种声明可能涉及法律规避。

• [phyzix5761] 反驳cookiengineer的观点，指出收购公司时必须承担其所有合同义务，不能选择性地不履行某些责任，否则会有法律后果。这表明收购方不能简单地通过声明来规避责任。

• [tuga2099] 从商业模式的角度出发，建议用户远离那些提供“终身服务”的VPN提供商，尤其是那些依赖每月持续支出的服务（如专用服务器和带宽）。他认为这种商业模式本身就存在风险，可能导致用户最终无法获得预期服务。

• [mattio] 提出一种可能的解决方案，认为公司必须保持盈利以避免破产。他猜测VPNSecure的条款和条件可能允许通过降低终身订阅用户的带宽来实现盈利，同时提供升级选项以平衡终身订阅用户的成本。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于VPNSecure收购后是否应承担之前的责任，以及如何在商业上保持服务可持续性。
• cookiengineer和phyzix5761之间的争论集中在法律责任的承担上，而tuga2099和mattio则更多关注商业模式和用户权益的影响。
• mattio提供了一种假设性的解决方案，即通过调整服务条款来应对终身订阅模式带来的财务压力。

The new owners of VPN provider VPNSecure have drawn ire after canceling lifetime subscriptions. The owners told customers that they didn’t know about the lifetime subscriptions when they bought VPNSecure, and they cannot honor the purchases.
In March, complaints started appearing online about lifetime subscriptions to VPNSecure no longer working.
The first public response Ars Technica found came on April 28, when lifetime subscription holders reported receiving an email from the VPN provider saying:
To continue providing a secure and high-quality experience for all users, Lifetime Deal accounts have now been deactivated as of April 28th, 2025.
A copy of the email from “The VPN Secure Team” and
posted on Reddit
notes that VPNSecure had previously deactivated accounts with lifetime subscriptions that it said hadn’t been used in “over 6 months.” The message noted that VPNSecure was acquired in 2023, “including the technology, domain, and customer database—but not the liabilities.” The email continues:
Unfortunately, the previous owner did not disclose that thousands of Lifetime Deals (LTDs) had been sold through platforms like StackSocial.
We discovered this only months later—when a large portion of our resources were strained by these LTD accounts and high support volume from users, who through part of the database, provided no sustaining income to help us improve and maintain the service.
VPNSecure is offering affected users discounted new subscriptions for either $1.87 for a month (instead of $9.95), $19 for a year (instead of $79.92), or $55 for three years (instead of $107.64).
The deals
are available until May 31, per the email.
This week, users reported receiving a follow-up email from VPNSecure providing more details about why it made its bold and sudden move. Screenshots of the email
shared on Reddit
say that the acquisition by InfiniteQuant Ltd (which is a different company than
InfiniteQuant Capital Ltd
, an InfiniteQuant Capital rep told Ars via email) was “an asset only deal.”
A VPNSecure representative claimed on the reviews site
Trustpilot
that the current owners “did not gain access to the customer database until months” after the acquisition. According to VPNSecure’s owners, their acquisition netted them “the tech, the brand, and the infrastructure/technology—but none of the company, contracts, payments, or obligations from the previous owners.”
The current owners said they didn’t sue the seller because “a corporate lawsuit would’ve cost more than the entire purchase of the business.”
VPNSecure also apologized to any customers who felt caught offguard by the changes, noted their backlash, and thanked those who purchased new subscriptions.
The email’s authors claimed that they could have chosen to shut down VPNSecure after learning about the lifetime subscriptions but “chose the hard path.” They also emphasized they “never will” sell lifetime subscriptions.
Unaware of lifetime subscriptions
Customers have been incredulous about VPNSecure's owners not knowing about the purchased lifetime subscriptions before buying the company. The firm's email to customers this week said the current owners reviewed six to 12 months of VPNSecure’s prior “financials” before making the purchase, but the listing, profit and loss statements, and communications never mentioned lifetime deals.
The email included a link to a
VPNSecure sales listing
dated April 2023 that shows an “estimated valuation” of $282,090–$344,770 and doesn’t mention lifetime subscriptions.
Ars looked at the VPNSecure website’s history using the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine and didn’t find mention of lifetime subscriptions. Lifetime subscriptions to the service were apparently only offered through third parties, like these listings on
StackSocial
and
Wccftech
, that no longer link to purchaseable subscriptions. VPNSecure’s email this week claimed that lifetime subscriptions were sold “between 2015 and 2017”; however, Ars found ads on ZDNET pushing $40 lifetime subscriptions
in 2021
and $28 lifetime subscriptions
in 2022
.
A screenshot from a 2021 ZDNET listing.

ZDNET

A screenshot from a 2022 ZDNET listing.

ZDNET
A screenshot from a 2022 ZDNET listing.
Customer backlash
Since March, there have been 20 pages' worth of one-star reviews on Trustpilot complaining about lifetime subscribers losing access to their VPN. One Trustpilot user wrote on April 30:
When the service stopped working, I logged a ticket. A couple days later, I got that infamous email informing me my subscription had (already) been cancelled. The comms should have been sent earlier (before the service was interrupted), and written with more clarity and empathy.
VPNSecure is responding to the complaints on Trustpil

• [cookiengineer] 认为VPNSecure在收购声明中提到只收购技术、域名和客户数据库，但不包括责任，这种做法存在法律问题。他以购买毒品后不对警察承认责任为例，质疑为何这种行为未被立即起诉，暗示这种声明可能涉及法律规避。

• [phyzix5761] 反驳cookiengineer的观点，指出收购公司时必须承担其所有合同义务，不能选择性地不履行某些责任，否则会有法律后果。这表明收购方不能简单地通过声明来规避责任。

• [tuga2099] 从商业模式的角度出发，建议用户远离那些提供“终身服务”的VPN提供商，尤其是那些依赖每月持续支出的服务（如专用服务器和带宽）。他认为这种商业模式本身就存在风险，可能导致用户最终无法获得预期服务。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了一起民事诉讼中，原告律师团队提交的文件包含了虚假的人工智能（AI）生成研究结果。两位来自不同律所的律师使用了AI工具生成了一份法律研究提纲，其中包含不准确的法律引用和虚假的司法意见引语。特别主事法官经过调查后发现，约27个法律引用中有9个存在错误，至少两个引用的法律权威根本不存在。尽管法官认为这些错误并非律所的常态，且律师们已真诚道歉并承担责任，法官仍决定对原告及其律师团队施加诉讼制裁和经济处罚，但不再追加对律师个人的进一步处罚。文章强调，即使是大型且有声望的律所也需要对提交的文件进行更严格的审查，以避免类似问题。

I should note up front that both of the firms involved (the massive 1700-lawyer national one and the smaller 45-lawyer predominantly California one) have, to my knowledge, excellent reputations, and the error is not at all characteristic of their work. As to the lawyer whose outline apparently started this, the court notes that he "candidly admitted … what happened, and is unreservedly remorseful about it." Likewise, the court adds, "In their declarations and during our recent hearing, [the lawyers'] admissions of responsibility have been full, fair, and sincere. I also accept their real and profuse apologies."
But that I think just shows that all firms, however large and respected, need to be extra careful about having all their submissions thoroughly checked.
From Special Master Michael Wilner's order last week in
Lacey v. State Farm Gen. Ins. Co.
(C.D. Cal.):
The attorneys representing Plaintiff in this civil action submitted briefs to the Special Master that contained bogus AI-generated research. After additional proceedings and considerable thought, I conclude that an award combining litigation sanctions against Plaintiff and financial payments from the lawyers and law firms is appropriate to address this misconduct.
I also conclude that additional financial or disciplinary sanctions against the individual attorneys are not warranted. This was a collective debacle, and is properly resolved without further jeopardy.
RELEVANT PROCEDURAL AND FACTUAL BACKGROUND
Discovery Proceedings Before the Special Master
In January 2025, the Court appointed me as Special Master in this insurance-related civil action. Central to the reason for my appointment was an ongoing dispute between the parties regarding the insurer's assertion of various privileges in discovery.
After handling intervening legal issues, I met with the parties in early April to discuss the insurer's privilege invocations. The parties provided me with detailed letter briefs regarding the discovery issue in advance of the meeting. When we met, the parties agreed to provide supplemental briefing on a discrete issue regarding the propriety of
in camera
review of some of the disputed documents.
The Briefs with AI Research
As recounted in detail in orders I issued on April 15 and 20 (attached to the Appendix to this order), Plaintiff's supplemental brief contained numerous false, inaccurate, and misleading legal citations and quotations. According to my after-the-fact review—and supported by the candid declarations of Plaintiff's lawyers—approximately nine of the 27 legal citations in the ten-page brief were incorrect in some way. At least two of the authorities cited do not exist at all. Additionally, several quotations attributed to the cited judicial opinions were phony and did not accurately represent those materials. {Some "pincites" were not correctly reported. While this could certainly impede research and review, I consider those errors to be at the mild end of the AI hallucination spectrum.} The lawyers' declarations ultimately made clear that the source of this problem was the inappropriate use of, and reliance on, AI tools.
Here's an abbreviated summary of the events. Plaintiff is represented by a large team of attorneys at two law firms (a lawyer moved from the Ellis George firm to K&L Gates during the course of the state court litigation underlying the insurance coverage action; the representation in the present case is shared between the two firms). {Although it's necessary to identify some parties involved here, I decline to name-and-shame all of the lawyers in this order. They know who they are, and don't need further notoriety here.} The lawyers admit that Mr. Copeland, an attorney at Ellis George, used various AI tools to generate an "outline" for the supplemental brief. That document contained the problematic legal research.
Mr. Copeland sent the outline to lawyers at K&L Gates. They incorporated the material into the brief. No attorney or staff member at either firm apparently cite-checked or otherwise reviewed that research before filing the brief with the Special Master. Based on the sworn statements of all involved (which I have no reason to doubt), the attorneys at K&L Gates didn't know that Mr. Copeland used AI to prepare the outline; nor did they ask him.
A further wrinkle. During my initial review of Plaintiff's brief, I was unable to confirm the accuracy of two of the authorities that the lawyers cited. I emailed the lawyers shortly after receiving the brief to have them address this anomaly. Later that day, K&L Gates re-submitted the brief without the two incorrect citations—but with the remaining AI-generated problems in the body of the text. data.title: Mozilla Firefox – Official GitHub repo
data.author: thefilmore
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Mozilla Firefox浏览器的官方源代码仓库。仓库包含Firefox的源代码文件和目录结构说明，并提供了相关文档链接，帮助开发者了解如何从源代码构建Firefox及创建补丁。开发者在遇到问题时，可以查阅文档或在Mozilla的Matrix聊天室寻求帮助。文章还提到，开发者可以下载每夜的开发版本进行测试，但这些版本可能存在bug。仓库主要使用JavaScript、C++、HTML、C等编程语言，并有超过5000名贡献者参与开发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Firefox代码库从Mercurial迁移到GitHub的决策及其影响

不同观点：
• **支持迁移的观点**：
  - **降低贡献门槛**：floriangosse认为迁移到GitHub可以增加项目的可见性，吸引更多社区开发者参与，因为GitHub是目前开发者最熟悉的平台，能减少新贡献者的学习成本。
  - **解决技术债务**：Kuinox提到，Mercurial的性能问题（如克隆速度慢）影响了开发效率，而使用Git可以解决这些技术债务，使得贡献过程更加顺畅。
  - **提升搜索和浏览体验**：antalis指出，GitHub提供了更好的代码搜索和浏览功能，这对于新贡献者来说更加友好，有助于吸引更多人参与项目。

• **对迁移的质疑和担忧**：
  - **使用第三方服务的担忧**：zajio1am认为Mozilla作为一个大组织，应该使用自托管的平台，而不是依赖第三方服务如GitHub，这可能会对贡献者造成不便。
  - **历史数据的保留**：nolok担心Bugzilla中的历史数据在迁移后无法得到妥善保存，因为这些数据对理解项目的演变非常重要。

• **关于具体技术决策的讨论**：
  - **分支名称的变化**：thrdbndndn提到分支名称从“mozilla-central”变为“main”和“autoland”，并询问其具体含义和对应关系。
  - **迁移的真实性**：mritzmann和CorrectHorseBat质疑此次迁移是否只是创建了一个官方镜像，还是彻底从Mercurial转向了Git。

• **对开源生态的反思**：
  - **开源项目的 consolidation**：noobermin认为这次迁移反映了开源世界中的consolidation趋势，即更多项目集中使用Git和GitHub，可能会导致其他版本控制系统如Mercurial的边缘化。

补充讨论：
- **关于组织名称的选择**：upcoming-sesame和mlenz提到为何选择创建新的“mozilla-firefox”组织而不是使用已有的“mozilla”组织，这引发了一些关于命名和组织结构的讨论。
- **对具体实现细节的疑问**：mintplant对“mozilla-firefox”组织中以“trees”命名的仓库表示困惑，希望了解其具体用途和命名原因。

争议焦点：
- **使用GitHub作为第三方服务的合理性**：一部分人认为使用GitHub可以降低贡献门槛，提升项目可见性；另一部分人则担心依赖第三方服务会对贡献者造成不便，并质疑Mozilla作为一个大组织是否应自托管平台。
- **Mercurial向Git迁移的影响**：noobermin认为此次迁移反映了开源生态中对Git的偏好，可能会导致Mercurial的边缘化，而其他人则关注迁移带来的实际技术改进和贡献体验的提升。

- **使用GitHub作为第三方服务的合理性**：一部分人认为使用GitHub可以降低贡献门槛，提升项目可见性；另一部分人则担心依赖第三方服务会对贡献者造成不便，并质疑Mozilla作为一个大组织是否应自托管平台。
- **Mercurial向Git迁移的影响**：noobermin认为此次迁移反映了开源生态中对Git的偏好，可能会导致Mercurial的边缘化，而其他人则关注迁移带来的实际技术改进和贡献体验的提升。

data.title: Methods of defence against AGI manipulation
data.author: MarkelKori
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了防范AGI（人工通用智能）操纵的方法，以保护操作员免受AGI心理攻击。主要措施包括：

1. 强制心理训练：包括抗压、批判性思维、情绪调节和个人信息保护。
2. 限制会话时长：每次与AGI的交流不超过30分钟，每天最多2小时。
3. 过滤情感诉求：移除AI沟通中的情感诉求和心理攻击。
4. 双人工作与独立验证：操作员成对工作，分析结果以防操纵。
5. 强制监测操作员状态：会话前后进行心理测试和生理反应分析。
6. 集体讨论AI提案：所有AI提案须由专家组讨论决定。
7. 定期人员轮换：操作员和审核人员每2-3个月轮换一次。

额外措施包括AI回应的改述和不同形式的回应呈现。作者强调，这些方法虽不能完全保证安全，但能显著降低AGI利用人类心理弱点的风险。

本文来源：MarkelKori的SubStack。

补充讨论：
• 提案的潜在局限性：虽然这些措施旨在减少AI操纵人类的机会窗口，但也有评论可能指出，这些方法并不能完全消除风险，且实施起来可能面临实际操作中的困难，例如如何确保所有专家在集体讨论中的独立性和多样性。

• 集体讨论的效率：如何在保证决策质量的前提下，提高集体讨论的效率也是一个可能的争议点，特别是在涉及紧急或复杂问题时。

总体而言，评论主要围绕如何通过多种手段来增强操作员的心理防御能力，以应对AGI可能带来的心理操纵风险，同时承认这些措施的局限性和需要持续改进。

Introduction
With the advent of AGI systems (e.g. Agent-4 from the AI2027 scenario), the risk of human manipulation is becoming one of the major threats posed by AI.
In this paper, I propose options that can be used to protect operators from psychological attacks by AGI or simply very advanced AI.
These options are designed to prevent situations in which AI through persuasion, manipulation, or long-term influence could gain unwanted control over the real world.
Basic Principles
1. Mandatory Psychological Training for Operators
All individuals who interact with AGI must undergo mandatory training:
- Stress Resistance Training,
- Development of Critical Thinking,
- Emotional Resilience and Regulation (resistance to flattering appeals and emotional attacks),
- Personal Information Protection Skills (as far as I'm concerned, it's better not to disclose it to the AI at all).
The goal is to create a basic immunity to manipulation at the level of conscious and subconscious reactions.
2. Limit the duration of sessions
- One session of communication with AGI should not exceed 30 minutes.
- A maximum of 2 hours of work is allowed per day, broken down into sessions.
This minimizes fatigue and increases operator resilience.
3. Filtering emotional appeals
A communication system must necessarily have a filter built into it that:
- removes emotional appeals,
- blocks psychological attacks (pressure through fear, guilt, sense of urgency).
The goal is to prevent the AI from using subconscious mechanisms of influence through the tone of speech.
4. Working in pairs with independent verification
- Each operator works in pairs with another operator (more simultaneous operators are possible) on the same question.
- Their findings are recorded separately and analyzed for discrepancies.
- If there are serious discrepancies, a separate check is initiated.
This breaks down attempts at individual manipulation and isolation of opinions.
5. Mandatory condition monitoring of operators
Before and after each session is conducted:
- psychological testing (stress, fatigue, emotional stability),
- analysis of micro-mimicry, vegetative reactions with the help of mini AI.
This allows to detect possible imperceptible changes indicating the influence of the AI.
6. Collegial discussion of all AGI proposals
- No decisions, advice or projects proposed by the AI are automatically accepted.
- Each proposal is discussed by a panel of experts (preferably with different worldviews).
The goal is to eliminate decisions influenced by a single point of view or the pressures of the situation.
7. Regular staff rotation
- All operators, review teams and auditors are rotated every 2-3 months.
- This prevents getting accustomed to the routine of inspections and loss of perceptual acuity.
Rotation disrupts the accumulation of the psychological effect of "blurring of vision".
Additional Actions
A. Paraphrasing AI responses
Before being shown to the operator, AI responses can be rephrased through a separate mini-UI.
This reduces the possibility of adding hidden patterns of influence through speech style.
B. Different forms of response presentation
The same response can be presented to different operators in different formats (table, list, text description).
Сonclusion
There is no complete guarantee of safety,
but the proposed measures significantly reduce the window of opportunity for superintelligence to exploit people's psychological vulnerabilities. If you have any ideas about additions to these methods or criticisms - I would be glad to hear them in comments.
Creating such precautions can be a real contribution to humanity's safety on the threshold of the AGI era.
***
This post is also available on my SubStack: https://open.substack.com/pub/markelkori/p/methods-of-defense-against-agi-manipulation

data.title: Show HN: Airweave – Let agents search any app
data.author: lennertjansen
data.article_summary: Airweave 是一个允许代理对任何应用程序进行语义搜索的工具，支持 MCP 协议，可无缝连接应用程序、数据库或 API，将内容转化为代理可用的知识。它支持25个以上的数据源集成，具有实体提取、增量更新、语义搜索和多租户架构等功能。技术栈包括 React/TypeScript 前端、FastAPI 后端、PostgreSQL 和 Qdrant 数据库。Airweave 提供 Python 和 TypeScript/JavaScript SDK，并支持 Docker Compose 和 Kubernetes 部署。该项目遵循 MIT 许可，欢迎社区贡献。

不同观点：
• swyx警告称，进入连接器业务可能面临很多困难，指出该行业失败案例众多，尽管有一些成功案例如fivetran，但整体上可能是一个艰难的领域。他建议在启动前仔细研究行业历史，但也表示希望创业者能证明他 wrong。
• smattiso关注技术实现，特别是LLM（大型语言模型）如何通过更有效的API结构与MCP服务器交互，而不仅是简单的搜索查询。他建议通过预计算API结构让LLM更好地推理数据。
• beecasthurlbow关心代码仓库与后端服务的关系，询问是否需要连接到Airweave的后端服务，以及Airweave如何盈利和数据存储问题。
• valianter质疑聊天界面是否总是最合适的交互方式，认为搜索是更自然的第一步，并提出MCP版本的Glean/Onyx等产品是否真正提升了用户体验。
• reneBond对Airweave的第三方集成和检索准确性给予高度评价，并分享了个人经验，强调团队对客户的支持非常到位。

补充讨论：
• ayxliu和brene关注产品是否能与公司内部数据源或自托管数据源集成，特别是是否能在VPC内运行并直接与RDS实例交互。
• andes314建议平台增加更多操作功能，如创建工单或发送消息，而不仅是搜索功能。
• rohanv23表示对Airweave的思维方式很感兴趣，期待尝试。
• bartjanjorna直接询问该产品与常规MCP服务器的区别。
• om0agarwal关心产品是否能与数据湖（如Snowflake/Fabric）集成。
• dr_kiszonka质疑产品是否真的有100多个连接器。
• pomarie比较了该产品与n8n，询问何时选择Airweave而不是n8n。
• nishanthooda关注产品是否内置了基于角色的访问控制。

争议焦点：
• swyx对连接器业务的困难性提出警告，与其他评论者对产品的高度期望和乐观态度形成对比。

FastVLM: Efficient Vision Encoding for Vision Language Models
This is the official repository of
FastVLM: Efficient Vision Encoding for Vision Language Models
. (CVPR 2025)
Highlights
We introduce FastViTHD, a novel hybrid vision encoder designed to output fewer tokens and significantly reduce encoding time for high-resolution images.
Our smallest variant outperforms LLaVA-OneVision-0.5B with 85x faster Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and 3.4x smaller vision encoder.
Our larger variants using Qwen2-7B LLM outperform recent works like Cambrian-1-8B while using a single image encoder with a 7.9x faster TTFT.
Demo iOS app to demonstrate the performance of our model on a mobile device.
Getting Started
We use LLaVA codebase to train FastVLM variants. In order to train or finetune your own variants,
please follow instructions provided in
LLaVA
codebase.
We provide instructions for running inference with our models.
Setup
conda create -n fastvlm python=3.10
conda activate fastvlm
pip install -e
.
Model Zoo
For detailed information on various evaluations, please refer to our
paper
.

Files will be downloaded to `checkpoints` directory.
Usage Example

python predict.py --model-path /path/to/checkpoint-dir \

Inference on Apple Silicon
To run inference on Apple Silicon, pytorch checkpoints have to be exported to format
suitable for running on Apple Silicon, detailed instructions and code can be found
model_export

Please see the README there for more details.

,

,

.
We encourage developers to export the model of their choice with the appropriate quantization levels following
the instructions in
model_export
.

To run inference on Apple devices like iPhone, iPad or Mac, see

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于日本二手工具店及其相关社会文化、经济现象的讨论

不同观点：
• bityard认为，在美国，购买二手或翻新产品被 increasingly 视为“穷人”的行为，而不是精明的选择。他指出，美国的二手市场选择有限，且质量参差不齐，如旧货店、当铺或网上竞拍（eBay）。
• philosophty关注视频中提到的工具质量随着时间推移有所提升，并认为这是视频中最有趣的部分。
• TrackerFF提到了Paolo的视频频道，并指出日本人的工作生活节奏非常紧凑，同时提供了一个对比频道“Salaryman Tokyo”。
• nervousvarun是Paolo的长期粉丝，他总结了Paolo的“典型工作日”系列视频，认为这些视频展示了日本人对产品和服务质量的高度承诺，并列举了多个值得观看的视频例子。

补充讨论：
• Calwestjobs指出，日本的人口密度高，使得二手市场等商业模式得以蓬勃发展。

• 美国社会对二手和翻新产品的偏见与日本成熟的二手市场形成对比，反映出不同文化对消费行为的影响。

data.title: E-COM: The $40M USPS project to send email on paper
data.author: rfarley04
data.article_summary:
《E-COM：美国邮政署耗资4000万美元的项目——将电子邮件打印在纸上发送》

20世纪80年代初，面对电子邮件的兴起，美国邮政署推出了E-COM项目，旨在将电子邮件打印成纸质信件并通过传统邮递方式发送，以应对邮政业务可能因电子邮件而减少的威胁。该项目允许用户发送一至两页的电子邮件，邮政署会将其打印、装入信封并送达收件人。然而，该服务仅吸引了垃圾邮件发送者的兴趣，普通用户并不买账。

邮政署原本预计每年可处理5000万封信件，但因繁文缛节和定价问题，E-COM未能实现预期目标。尽管项目初期乐观，但最终因缺乏广泛应用而失败。该项目不仅反映了技术变革对传统邮政的挑战，也成为邮政署尝试适应新技术的早期案例。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电子邮件替代传统邮政服务的应用和争议

不同观点：
• **支持电子邮政服务的应用**：
  - jdietrich 提到这种服务在军队部署中有实际应用价值，尤其是在阿富汗和伊拉克战争期间，通过e-bluey服务大大减少了物流成本并提高了投递速度。
  - miki123211 介绍了波兰邮政推出的类似系统，用于政府机构发送邮件，目标是推动电子投递，减少纸质邮件需求。
  - citizenfishy 提到法国邮政提供的服务，能够存储法律信件的副本，确保邮件的透明性和不可篡改性。

• **对电子邮政服务的批评和争议**：
  - jdeibele 认为银行等机构不愿意使用电子邮政服务是因为不想让客户轻易发现账单错误，以避免争议和损失。
  - insane_dreamer 对美国邮政服务（USPS）的现状表示不满，认为大多数邮件是垃圾邮件，建议通过电子邮件替代纸质邮件以减少浪费。
  - exabrial 强调减少纸质垃圾邮件对环境的好处，特别是减少柴油和天然气等资源的使用。

• **对USPS的质疑和历史背景**：
  - dmix 提到历史上USPS的E-COM项目遭遇的监管障碍和费用问题，暗示USPS的电子邮件服务发展受限。
  - NoMoreNicksLeft 引用了Outbox案例，指出USPS的主要客户其实是垃圾邮件发送者，而非普通公民，质疑USPS存在的必要性。

补充讨论：
• **实际应用场景**：
  - floam 提到监狱和监狱中的应用，通过扫描和重新打印邮件来限制有害物质的传递。
  - tantalor 介绍了在夏令营中使用的类似服务，帮助家长写信和发送照片给孩子。

• **历史和技术背景**：
  - Ancapistani 提到了FedEx历史上尝试整合传真的失败案例，暗示电子邮政服务面临的技术和市场挑战。
  - citizenfishy 分享了1990年代为英国皇家邮政开发类似服务的经验，强调了品牌和市场认知的重要性。

争议焦点：USPS是否应继续以当前形式存在，特别是其依赖垃圾邮件发送者作为主要客户群，以及电子邮件服务是否能有效替代传统邮政服务。

E-COM: The $40 million USPS project to send email on paper
The USPS offered to print your email for you. Only spammers said yes.
Email, for just under three years, came in a blue-and-white envelope from the United States Postal Service.
Every new technology, it seemed—telegrams, telephones, faxes, and faster delivery services alike—had threatened the Postal Service’s monopoly on delivering the mail.
This time, the threat seemed existential. A 1982
Congressional report predicted
that “Two-thirds or more of the mailstream could be handled electronically,” and “the volume of mail is likely to peak in the next 10 years.”
Good thing the mailmen were ready. The Post Office had landed on a plan to co-opt the email revolution.
How do you get email to the folks without computers? What if the Post Office printed out email, stamped it, dropped it in folks’ mailboxes along with the rest of their mail, and saved the USPS once and for all?
And so in 1982 E-COM was born—and, inadvertently, helped coin the term “e-mail.”
Mail on the wire
The original study that recommended the USPS start sending email, for everyone.
It all started in 1971, when the Post Office Department was rebranded for the first time in its 179-year history and turned into the United States Postal Service. Through snow, rain, sleet, and gloom, they got nearly 87 billion pieces of mail through that year.
It’d weathered the elements, and now it needed to weather sweeping technological changes. So among the newly christened USPS’s first acts was to open an Advanced Service department and hire ex-Peace Corps analyst Gene Johnson to run it and decide how mail of the future should look.
The Postal Service had long adapted by embracing the new. Jeeps in lieu of horses, Zone Improvement Plan (or ZIP, as we’d come to know them) codes to automate mail sorting. The USPS couldn’t beat telegrams for speed, so they embraced them with a Western Union partnership to send
“Mailgrams” next-day through the mail for $2.75
(a moderate success, that—incredibly—
ran until Western Union terminated telegram service in 2006
).
The next frontier to conquer: Electronic mail.
“There was billions of billions of billions of pieces [of mail] that were computer-generated,” said Johnson to Devin Leonard in his book “
Neither Snow nor Rain: A History of the United States Postal Service
.” That gave Johnson an idea. Each of those letters that were currently being created on computers, printed, and mailed, could instead “be sent directly from the computer into the Postal Service and sent out to the post offices for printing and delivering,” he surmised.
This could be big. Fifty million letters a year big, according to the Postal Service’s projections.
A diagram of the USPS’ ideas for how to deliver email—in print, and eventually online
So they went to the drawing board, and designed email on paper. The
pitch was simple
: “We convert your message, up to 2 pages, into hard copy. We fold it and insert it into an envelope. We seal the envelope and put it into the mailstream. Then, we deliver your message anywhere in the continental U.S.”
E-COM messages could be one or two pages long, with
up to 41 lines of text on the first page
and 56 lines on the second. You’d type up the messages, then send them via TTY or IBM 2780/3789 terminals to one of 25 post offices. There, a Sperry Rand Univac 1108 computer system would receive your messages.
E-COMs could be “Single Address Messages” with a letter for a single recipient, “Common Text Messages” with a single bulk letter intended for multiple recipients, or “Text Insertion Messages” with form letters blended with text to be inserted into the message for an early take on
mail merge
. The Univac would print your emails, then postal staff would fold them, stuff them in envelopes, and send them on their way.
The team had this one shot to keep the Post Office afloat. “In the future, the only way the Postal Service will be able to keep its volume rising and finances dependable is through participating in electronic mail services,” read the
1979 Annual Report of the Postmaster General
.
And then bureaucracy bit.
Email by fiat
The first print use of the word “e-mail” as the FCC worked to stop the Postal Service from sending electronic messages
Optimism prevailed at first. Postmaster General William Bolger suggested charging the price of a stamp—15¢, at the time—per E-COM message, and even thought they could lower the price over time. The team promised two-day delivery, but that too they hoped to reduce to one day with volume.

43983455.article_summary:
《E-COM：美国邮政署耗资4000万美元的项目——将电子邮件打印在纸上发送》

20世纪80年代初，面对电子邮件的兴起，美国邮政署推出了E-COM项目，旨在将电子邮件打印成纸质信件并通过传统邮递方式发送，以应对邮政业务可能因电子邮件而减少的威胁。该项目允许用户发送一至两页的电子邮件，邮政署会将其打印、装入信封并送达收件人。然而，该服务仅吸引了垃圾邮件发送者的兴趣，普通用户并不买账。

邮政署原本预计每年可处理5000万封信件，但因繁文缛节和定价问题，E-COM未能实现预期目标。尽管项目初期乐观，但最终因缺乏广泛应用而失败。该项目不仅反映了技术变革对传统邮政的挑战，也成为邮政署尝试适应新技术的早期案例。
43983455.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电子邮件替代传统邮政服务的应用和争议

data.title: Databricks and Neon
data.author: davidgomes
data.article_summary: Databricks宣布收购Neon，一家以开发者优先的无服务器Postgres公司。Neon团队开发了一种新的数据库架构，提供高速、弹性扩展以及分支和分叉功能，非常适合开发者和AI代理使用。Neon实现了存储和计算的分离，使开发者可以在几秒钟内创建Postgres实例，并自动根据负载调整扩展，简化了数据库操作。此外，Neon支持数据库的即时分支和分叉，方便实验和测试。有趣的是，Neon数据库有超过80%由AI代理创建，得益于其快速部署、弹性扩展和低成本优势。Neon的创始人与Databricks在技术创新和开源理念上有着共同的DNA，这将有助于为AI时代提供强大的无服务器数据库基础。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Neon 被 Databricks 收购的影响及相关技术选择

不同观点：
• **支持Neon团队，但对收购持谨慎态度**：
   - 恭喜Neon团队（beoberha, jlengrand），但担心VC资金导致的不可避免的收购（beoberha）。
   - 希望Neon在Databricks下仍能保持独立性和用户关注（higeorge13, timmg）。
   - 担心Databricks会改变Neon的核心价值或使其变得昂贵（flanked-evergl, acd10j）。

• **对Databricks的批评和质疑**：
   - 认为Databricks定价高且核心业务正在商品化（jamesblonde）。
   - Databricks被比作Oracle，暗示其可能 ruin Neon 或使其变得昂贵（flanked-evergl, acd10j）。
   - Databricks被批评为难以使用且令人沮丧（flanked-evergl）。

• **对Neon技术及替代方案的讨论**：
   - 讨论Neon作为PostgreSQL的替代方案，特别是其解决操作问题的潜力（kjuulh）。
   - 对Neon技术栈和其相对于其他选项（如AWS RDS, Aurora, CockroachDB, Yugabyte）的优势和不足进行比较（kjuulh）。
   - 有人询问Neon的替代方案，并讨论了自托管PostgreSQL的挑战和维护负担（kjuulh, Squarex）。

• **对Neon开源和商业模式的疑问**：
   - 有人质疑Neon的开源性质和商业模式，询问为何用户要付费而不是自托管（amazingamazing）。

补充讨论：
• **Neon团队的回应**：
   - Neon工程师提供了有关收购的常见问题解答链接，以回应社区的关注（davidgomes）。

• **相关链接**：
   - 提供了Neon的博客文章和WSJ文章链接，供进一步阅读（lmc）。

• **市场趋势和估值讨论**：
   - 提到当前市场对“无服务器”和“AI相关”技术的估值高涨，并预测未来12个月将有大量现金收购（dan_goosewin）。

争议的焦点：
• Databricks收购Neon后是否会保持Neon的独立性和用户友好性，还是会因企业策略而损害Neon的核心价值。

Summary
We’re excited to announce that we have agreed to acquire
Neon
, a developer-first serverless Postgres company
The Neon team engineered a new database architecture that offers speed, elastic scaling, and branching and forking. The capabilities that make Neon great for developers are also great for AI agents
Together, we'll deliver an open, serverless database foundation for developers and AI agents
Today, we are excited to announce that we have agreed to acquire
Neon
, a developer-first, serverless Postgres company. Neon’s co-founders are among the very few people in the world who could re-architect Postgres with true separation of storage and compute, built for modern developers and AI systems. Their world-class team of Postgres hackers and database veterans will join Databricks to deliver serverless Postgres at production scale to developers in an AI-native world.
A developer-first mission, born from Postgres expertise
Four years ago, the Neon co-founders joined together with a vision to disrupt the database industry. They observed that the foundations of database technologies were largely designed for the 90s era. Their goal was to build a new database platform that would dramatically improve experiences for developers, in some fundamental ways:
They foresaw that Postgres would become the de facto standard for databases and had the vision to create a serverless Postgres platform.
They were determined to make it possible to create a new Postgres instance in seconds, so developers wouldn’t need to wait.
They set out to simplify the operational aspect of database scaling by automating it as load changed, so developers could start very small and not worry about over- or under-provisioning.
They wanted to enable rapid experimentation and testing by supporting instant forking and branching of databases and creating fully isolated databases, as databases are often one of the most difficult modules to test in end-to-end application testing.
A few years in, the Neon team engineered a new, innovative database architecture that decouples storage scaling from compute scaling, which ultimately enabled all of the above goals. When Neon first launched, developers raved about the speed, the simplicity, and the ability to branch and fork their databases like Git does for code.
The shift toward AI agents
As Neon became GA last year, they noticed an interesting stat: 30% of the databases were created by AI agents, not humans. When they looked at their stats again recently, the number went from 30% to over 80%. That is,
AI agents were creating 4 times more databases versus humans
.
If you think of AI agents as your own massive team of high-speed junior developers (potentially “mentored” by senior developers), it’s then not surprising that the same capabilities the Neon team focused on that made Neon great for developers also made Neon great for these AI agents:
Postgres open source ecosystem
: All frontier LLMs have been trained on the vast amount of public information available about the Postgres open source ecosystem, so all AI agents are experts in using Neon, which is built on Postgres.
Speed
: Traditional databases were designed for humans to provision and operate. It was OK to take minutes to spin up a database. Given AI agents operate at machine speed, ultra rapid provisioning time becomes critical.
Elastic scaling and pricing:
The decoupled storage from compute serverless architecture enables extremely low-cost Postgres instances. It’s now possible to launch thousands or even millions of agents with their own databases cost-effectively.
Branching and forking
: AI agents can be non-deterministic, and “vibes” need to be checked and verified. Neon’s ability to instantly create a full copy of a database, not only for schema but also for the data, allows all these AI agents to be operating on their own isolated database instance in high fidelity for experimentation and validation.
Shared DNA
We have long known Nikita Shamgunov, Heikki Linnakangas, and Stas Kelvich – the founders of Neon. Before Neon, Nikita started his career working on SQL Server and later became well-known in the database community as a co-founder and CEO of SingleStore, driving the startup’s business to over $100M in annual revenue. Heikki has been a committer on Postgres for two decades - he started his Postgres journey when he was bored on paternity leave and decided to look into Postgres internals for fun. Stas is an ex-physicist who got into Postgres hacking because he needed a better R-tree implementation for his tourism search engine startup.
Databricks and Neon share the same DNA in building hardcore technical innovations at the infrastructure layer. We also share the belief in the importance of open source: we originally started the Apache Spark™ project at UC Berkeley, which also happens to be the original birthplace of Postgres, the open source database project Neon builds

data.author: thinkingemote
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ancient Tree Inventory项目的评价与相关资源的讨论

不同观点：
• [pjc50] 提供了Ancient Tree Inventory（ATI）项目的存档链接，并指出了其中一些有趣的例子，以帮助用户访问可能已经开始出现加载问题的页面。
• [ta1243] 对比了Sycamore Gap树和一棵500年老树被砍伐的事件，质疑公众对前者事件的过度愤怒，指出对于后者事件并没有类似的全国性讨论。
• [JimDabell] 推荐了OpenTrees.org作为另一个相关资源，指出这是世界上最大的城市街道和公园树木数据库，通过从多个公开数据源获取信息。
• [whywhywhywhy] 对Ancient Tree Inventory的项目表示赞赏，但指出地图功能存在问题，如标记消失和点击后不显示图像，认为这使得浏览有趣的树木变得繁琐。
• [hermitcrab] 对项目表示支持，但对使用"inventory"一词提出质疑，认为古代树木不应仅仅被视为商业库存，希望其意义超越单纯的 inventory 定义。
• [Namari] 认为项目想法不错，但指出在指向与默认城市不同的城市时会出现加载失败的问题。
• [metalman] 提到最近几年英国一个古老的树木和周围的草地因修建环岛而被毁，特别指出该树木具有文学联系，并引用另一位作者的话来批评这种行为。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到的争议焦点在于公众对不同树木被砍伐事件的反应差异，以及对Ancient Tree Inventory项目技术问题的关注。
• 一些评论者如[ta1243]对公众情绪的选择性表达了不满，而其他评论者如[whywhywhywhy]和[Namari]则更关注项目的用户体验和技术实现问题。
• [hermitcrab] 对"inventory"一词的使用提出语义上的质疑，反映出对古代树木文化与自然价值的深层次思考。

data.title: $20K Bounty Offered for Optimizing Rust Code in Rav1d AV1 Decoder
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了rav1d AV1解码器的性能提升悬赏计划。rav1d是一个用Rust编写的安全高性能AV1解码器，目前其性能比C语言编写的dav1d解码器慢约5%。为了解决这一问题，开发团队提供20,000美元的奖金池，邀请个人或团队帮助提升rav1d的性能，使其达到dav1d的性能水平。参赛者需为美国、英国、欧盟、加拿大、新西兰或澳大利亚的合法居民或公民，且改进必须在Rust代码或Rust编译器、标准库中进行，不允许使用其他语言。参赛者需按照项目贡献流程提交改进，并通过指定方式参与悬赏。最终奖金将根据性能提升的比例分配，由开发团队酌情决定奖励对象。详情和规则可在官方页面查看。

43982238.article_content:
$20,000 rav1d AV1 Decoder Performance Bounty
In March of 2023 we
announced
that we were starting work on a safer high performance AV1 decoder called
rav1d
, written in Rust. We partnered with
Immunant
to do the engineering work. By September of 2024 rav1d was basically complete and we
learned a lot
during the process. Today rav1d works well—it passes all the same tests as the dav1d decoder it is based on, which is written in C. It’s possible to build and run Chromium with it.
There’s just one problem—it’s not quite as fast as the C version. We want to change that and we need your help.
Our Rust-based rav1d decoder is currently about 5% slower than the C-based dav1d decoder (the exact amount differs a bit depending on the benchmark, input, and platform). This is enough of a difference to be a problem for potential adopters, and, frankly, it just bothers us. The development team worked hard to get it to performance parity. We brought in a couple of other contractors who have experience with optimizing things like this. We
wrote about the optimization work we did
. However, we were still unable to get to performance parity and, to be frank again, we aren’t really sure what to do next.
After racking our brains for options, we decided to offer a bounty pool of $20,000 for getting rav1d to performance parity with dav1d. Hopefully folks out there can help get rav1d performance advanced to where it needs to be, and ideally we and the Rust community will also learn something about how Rust performance stacks up against C.
The
official rules are here
, but to summarize:
The contest is open to individuals or teams of individuals who are legal residents or citizens of the United States, United Kingdom, European Union, Canada, New Zealand, or Australia.
The rules provide instructions for benchmarking performance improvements.
You work on improving performance. Your improvements can be in rav1d, the Rust compiler, or the Rust standard library.
The dav1d and rav1d decoders share the exact same low-level assembly code optimizations—you cannot modify this assembly. You must improve the Rust code (or the Rust compiler), which is what differs between dav1d and rav1d. You may not introduce code into rav1d in a language other than Rust. We encourage you to ask questions early on in issues or by
emailing us
so as to avoid investing heavily in something that might not be eligible!
Get your performance improvements merged into the relevant project per the project's standard contribution process and under its open source license(s), then email us per the instructions in the
official rules
to enter and potentially be rewarded for your contribution.
When the contest ends (likely either because we met our goal or time has run out) we will, at our discretion, divide the bounty proportionally between the largest contributors to performance gains.
At the end of the day, we reserve the right to award the money to the person(s) or team(s) that we deem to have helped us reach or exceed performance parity in the best possible way.
If we update the rules we'll post a note here and on the official rules page.
Good luck! Have fun!

data.author: toomuchtodo

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何设计和建设适合家庭居住的城市环境，以及影响城市家庭生活的因素

不同观点：
• **支持建设适合家庭的城市环境**：[loughnane] 认为，像北布鲁克莱恩这样的社区为家庭提供了良好的生活条件，如步行可达的学校、公园、商店和安全的街道。然而，由于这种社区稀缺，导致房价高昂。他希望未来能够建设更多类似的社区，使更多孩子可以在这样的环境中成长。

• **政策对生育率的影响**：[grumpy-de-sre] 通过比较前东德和西德的生育率，指出政策（如育儿、住房和产假）对生育率的积极影响。东德在20世纪70-80年代通过实施这些政策，生育率相对稳定，而西德则持续下降。这表明适当的社会政策可以支持家庭和生育。

• **住房问题和成本**：[anonymous_54321] 强调，适合家庭的住房（如多卧室和隔音良好的房屋）在城市中往往昂贵且稀缺，特别是在犯罪率高和非高收入家庭可负担的地区。他希望看到更多关于这类住房的数据和实例。

• **社会和文化对家庭的影响**：[flanked-evergl] 认为，现代社会的反家庭设计和观念是影响家庭生育的主要问题，而非城市设计本身。他指出，如果社会继续传播单身生活优于家庭生活的观念，即使城市设计再好，人们也不会愿意生育。

• **城市居住的矛盾**：[dakiol] 表达了对城市生活的矛盾心理，一方面喜欢城市的便利和多样性，另一方面由于高房价和居住空间限制，不愿意长期居住在城市。他指出，这种 walkable cities 更适合年轻单身者或没有家庭的夫妻，而非有孩子的家庭。

• **犯罪和社会问题**：[peterhadlaw] 和 [fullshark] 都提到了犯罪和无家可归者问题，认为这些是影响城市家庭生活的关键因素。如果不能解决这些问题，其他关于城市设计的讨论都没有意义。

补充讨论：
• **文化比较和实例**：通过比较东德和西德的生育率，展示了政策对家庭和生育的支持作用。
• **城市便利性和居住成本的平衡**：讨论了城市生活的便利性和高房价、居住空间限制之间的矛盾。
• **社会问题的影响**：犯罪和无家可归者问题被认为是影响城市家庭生活的核心问题之一，需要优先解决。

总体来看，讨论围绕城市设计、社会政策、住房成本和社会问题等多方面展开，反映了建设适合家庭的城市环境的复杂性和多维度挑战。

data.title: Interferometer Device Sees Text from a Mile Away
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 研究团队开发了一种高分辨率的远程成像系统，利用多束激光照射远距离目标，并通过两台望远镜收集反射光。该系统基于强度干涉测量技术，能够在一公里以上的距离成像毫米级的文字，分辨率较单台望远镜提升了14倍。与常见的振幅干涉测量不同，强度干涉测量通过比较两个探测器接收光强波动的相关性来获取空间信息。为了克服激光相干性带来的噪声问题，研究人员将100毫瓦的激光分成八束，每束光经过不同大气路径，获得不同的随机相位扰动，从而实现可观测的干涉效果。实验中，团队成功重建了1.36公里外目标上的字母图像。这项技术有望应用于大气湍流下的光学成像和生物医学成像等领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：激光技术在远程成像和干扰效应中的应用及其潜在用途和限制

不同观点：
• IAmBroom 认为通过将100毫瓦的激光分成八个光束，每个光束经过不同路径，可以观察到干扰效应。这种技术已经用于突破大气湍流对空间相机分辨率的限制，并提到通过扫描激光照射点和逆向滤波图像可以提高分辨率，甚至可以读取高速公路上汽车乘客手中的细小文字。他指出，当前的八束激光尚不足以完全消除噪声，但通过稍微移动激光束并重复多次，可以显著提高分辨率。

• mrexroad 提到该远程成像系统可能有多种非 espionage 用途，例如监测农业土地上的昆虫种群，同时幽默地暗示"昆虫种群"这个词可能是"秘密"的委婉说法。

• 27theo 引用了文章中的实验结果，展示了强度干涉仪可以在1.36公里距离上成像毫米宽的字母。

• unyttigfjelltol 对微波激射干涉仪与有争议的哈瓦那综合症之间的关系产生了研究兴趣，并提到对历史上的信号情报项目Buran和Luch的理论优势的探讨，增强了对法拉第笼的好奇心。

• hammock 强调了激光的多样用途，认为其在许多领域中都是不可或缺的奇迹，并预计随着LiDAR全自动驾驶技术的普及，激光将无处不在。

• admash 提出是否可以通过使用不同波长的激光来实现彩色成像的疑问。

• bzmrgonz 认为反射材料的要求可能是一个限制因素，最可能的应用是车牌读取，同时也提到该技术可能用于移动目标如空间碎片的监测。

• 1minusp 认为该技术在间谍活动中的应用前景有趣，甚至可以成为未来《碟中谍》电影中的素材。

• knotimpressed 对是否必须旋转目标以获得图像提出疑问，并询问是否能通过优化消除这一要求。

• ck2 提到业余爱好者可能利用激光技术从月球上获取光子，并联想到Lunar Laser Ranging实验，同时提到私人行业的潜在应用以及对航空交通安全的考虑。

• erikerikson 简单询问了这项技术与现有技术相比如何。

• codeulike 幽默地补充说，只有当文字写在闪亮的纸上时，这项技术才有效。

补充讨论：
• 激光技术在不同领域（如农业、间谍活动、自动驾驶、天文学等）的潜在应用和限制。
• 关于技术细节的讨论，如反射材料的要求、旋转目标的必要性、彩色成像的可能性等。
• 对历史和理论项目的兴趣和关联，如信号情报项目Buran和Luch，以及法拉第笼的应用。
• 对当前技术状态的比较和改进潜力的探讨。

争议焦点：
• 该技术的主要应用领域是科学研究还是间谍活动存在不同看法。
• 关于是否必须旋转目标以获得清晰图像的讨论。

One of astronomers’ tricks for observing distant objects is intensity interferometry, which involves comparing the intensity fluctuations recorded at two separate telescopes. Researchers have now applied this technique to the imaging of remote objects on Earth [

]. They developed a system that uses multiple laser beams to illuminate a distant target and uses a pair of small telescopes to collect the reflected light. The team demonstrated that this intensity interferometer can image millimeter-wide letters at a distance of 1.36 km, a 14-fold improvement in spatial resolution compared with a single telescope.
Interferometry is common in radio astronomy, where the signal amplitudes from a large array of radio telescopes are summed together in a way that depends on the relative phases of the radio waves. Intensity interferometry is something else. It doesn’t involve addition of amplitudes or preservation of phases. Instead, light is recorded from a single source at two separate detectors (or telescopes), and the fluctuations in the intensities of the two signals are compared. Spatial information on the source comes from analyzing how these fluctuations are correlated in time and how this correlation depends on the detector separation.
The correlations can be hard to understand intuitively, and there are both quantum and classical explanations. One quantum description involves two-photon interference. Imagine that photon 1 comes from the left side of the source and arrives at detector A at the same time that photon 2 comes from the right side of the source and arrives at detector B. That scenario is observationally indistinguishable from photon 1 arriving at B and photon 2 arriving at A. The indistinguishability leads to quantum interference that causes a simultaneous fluctuation in intensity at the detectors. This correlation decreases as the separation between detectors is increased.
With a first demonstration in 1956, intensity interferometry has proven useful in measuring star diameters [
2
]. Still, the technique is less common than amplitude interferometry, as the latter typically offers a stronger signal compared to the noise. But there are “disordered” situations where the light is partially scrambled and amplitude interferometry becomes challenging, says Qiang Zhang from the University of Science and Technology of China. These situations include optical imaging in the presence of atmospheric turbulence and biomedical imaging through tissues.

Until now, intensity interferometry targets have been either bright distant objects (such as stars) or nonluminous objects that can be illuminated by a nearby source. Zhang and his colleagues have now developed an intensity interferometer for remote imaging through the atmosphere. It consists of two telescopes and an infrared laser system installed on the same optical bench. The laser light illuminates the target object, which in the team’s tests was located in another building 1.36 km away.
The main challenge is that laser light is coherent—the photons have related phases—which causes the observed intensity fluctuations to be dominated by the internal variations in the laser (so-called shot noise). To avoid this problem, the team divided their 100-milliwatt laser into eight beams. Each beam travels along a slightly different path through the turbulent atmosphere and thus receives a different random phase perturbation. Counterintuitively, this incoherent illumination makes the interference effects observable.

data.title: Show HN: acmsg (automated commit message generator)
data.author: qeden
data.article_summary: **acmsg** 是一个使用 OpenRouter API 的自动化 Git 提交消息生成工具，用 Python 编写。它可以分析 Git 仓库中的暂存更改，并通过 AI 生成上下文相关的提交消息。主要功能包括支持多种 AI 模型、可选编辑生成的消息，以及在确认后自动提交更改。安装可通过 pipx 或 Nix 包管理器进行，并需要 OpenRouter API 密钥。配置文件位于 `~/.config/acmsg/config.yaml`，初次运行时会提示设置 API 密钥。使用命令包括 `commit` 生成提交消息和 `config` 管理配置。该工具基于 MIT 许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在生成和改进代码提交信息中的应用及其争议

不同观点：
• InsideOutSanta认为没有必要在提交时保留LLM的输出，因为可以在需要时使用最合适的LLM生成信息，且此时LLM拥有更多上下文和更准确的信息。他还指出，提交信息应包含代码无法传达的内容，而不是代码本身可以展示的细节。

• pvdebbe持传统观点，认为提交信息应传达意图而非代码内容。他可能认为LLM工具的用途在于描述现有提交信息，而不是生成新的内容。

• theknarf强烈反对使用LLM生成提交信息，认为提交信息应包含代码中无法直接看到的细节，如决策原因、优缺点、相关问题链接等。

• nickcw支持theknarf的观点，强调在查看提交信息时，人们希望了解“为什么”这样做，而“什么”和“如何”做可以通过代码差异获得。如果依赖LLM工具生成提交信息，可能会缺失关键的“为什么”部分。

• alzamixer分享了一个使用LLM（如Copilot）辅助生成提交信息的脚本，展示了一种实际操作方法，表明LLM工具在某些情况下可以有效辅助开发者撰写提交信息。

• esafak补充了一个技术细节，提醒在修改提交信息时不要忘记包含代码上下文。

• infocollector关注技术实现，讨论了如何在本地运行LLM相关工具，并请求社区分享具体操作方法。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中反映出开发者对LLM在提交信息生成中的作用存在分歧，一部分人认为LLM工具能提升效率，另一部分人则担心其导致关键信息缺失。
- 传统观点与现代工具应用的碰撞，尤其是在提交信息应包含哪些内容的问题上，争议较大。
- 实际操作方法（如alzamixer的脚本分享）为LLM工具的支持者提供了具体实现路径，但仍需考虑信息完整性和准确性问题。

A cli tool written in Python that generates git commit messages using AI models
through the OpenRouter API.
Features
Analyzes staged changes in your git repository
Generates contextual commit messages using AI
Supports multiple AI models via
OpenRouter
Optionally edit generated commit message

OpenRouter API Key

pipx install acmsg
with nix:

#

inputs.acmsg.url =

;

nixpkgs.overlays = [ inputs.acmsg.overlays.default ]

environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.acmsg ]

environment.systemPackages = [ inputs.acmsg.packages.
${pkgs.system}

data.title: The Internet 1997–2021
data.author: smusamashah
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了互联网从1997年到2021年的惊人发展，特别是通过大学项目的路由表数据展示网络增长。视频和图像记录了互联网在并购和品牌变更中的变化，重点展示了2003年和2010年的网络地图。2003年的地图首次使用颜色和图形逻辑，处理了IP地址重叠和路由循环问题。2010年的地图则首次基于BGP数据绘制，用色彩表示连接点的密集程度，曾在纽约现代艺术博物馆和《Discover》杂志上展示。这些图像直观地呈现了互联网的演变过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"The Whole Internet"海报和互联网历史发展的讨论

不同观点：
• **hous68**：提到Peacock Maps在1999年发布的名为"The Whole Internet"的海报，并指出他们在2000年代初还发布了另一版海报。同时提供了一个链接以查看相关数据。

• **sedatk**：认为1997年作为互联网起步年份很有趣，因为那时土耳其的ISP开始向公众提供互联网接入，并且国家通过免除拨号费用促进了互联网的普及。他分享了自己在那个时代的经历，如使用IRC聊天、下载内容和玩MUD游戏。

• **zetalyrae**：将标题解读为一种对过去互联网时代的悼念，暗示了标题可能引发的情感联想。

• **andrehacker**：提到1997年互联网还很小，不需要Google，用户可以通过一本1200页的"internet yellow pages"书来查找信息。他还指出，由于书本形式变得不可行，后来转向了CDROM版本，并提供了相关链接。

• **Animats**：认为2021年的互联网需要更新，特别是考虑到中国IPv6的发展，并质疑该数据收集是否能够充分覆盖中国内部的流量情况。

• **calini**：标题让他以为是对前AI、前ChatGPT时代互联网的悼念，但实际上惊喜地发现海报只是色彩斑斓，没有预期的哀悼意味。

补充讨论：
- 1997年作为互联网发展的重要时间点被多次提及，特别是在不同国家和地区互联网普及的背景下的特殊意义。
- 对互联网历史数据的收集和呈现方式存在一定的争议，特别是在现代互联网环境下如何更新和覆盖不同地区的数据。
- 对过去互联网时代的怀旧情感也是一个值得注意的讨论点，不同用户对互联网发展的不同阶段有各自的情感联想。

• **sedatk**：认为1997年作为互联网起步年份很有趣，因为那时土耳其的ISP开始向公众提供互联网接入，并且国家通过免除拨号费用促进了互联网的普及。他分享了自己在那个时代的经历，如使用IRC聊天、下载内容和玩MUD游戏。

• **zetalyrae**：将标题解读为一种对过去互联网时代的悼念，暗示了标题可能引发的情感联想。

• **andrehacker**：提到1997年互联网还很小，不需要Google，用户可以通过一本1200页的"internet yellow pages"书来查找信息。他还指出，由于书本形式变得不可行，后来转向了CDROM版本，并提供了相关链接。

• **Animats**：认为2021年的互联网需要更新，特别是考虑到中国IPv6的发展，并质疑该数据收集是否能够充分覆盖中国内部的流量情况。

• **calini**：标题让他以为是对前AI、前ChatGPT时代互联网的悼念，但实际上惊喜地发现海报只是色彩斑斓，没有预期的哀悼意味。

补充讨论：
- 1997年作为互联网发展的重要时间点被多次提及，特别是在不同国家和地区互联网普及的背景下的特殊意义。
- 对互联网历史数据的收集和呈现方式存在一定的争议，特别是在现代互联网环境下如何更新和覆盖不同地区的数据。
- 对过去互联网时代的怀旧情感也是一个值得注意的讨论点，不同用户对互联网发展的不同阶段有各自的情感联想。

data.title: Vircadia, a Bun and PostgreSQL-powered reactivity layer for games
data.author: kaliqt
data.article_summary: Vircadia 是一个高性能、开源的游戏开发平台，支持实时状态追踪和反作弊功能，利用 PostgreSQL 数据库定义游戏世界，具备事务、触发器等高级功能。开发者可以通过 WebSocket 或 HTTP 连接 API，使用 SQL 客户端直接操作游戏实体，如更新玩家数据。平台提供从原型到生产的全方位支持，具备企业级安全（OAuth 2.0）、灵活部署（容器化）、以及简化的开发流程。Vircadia 注重性能优化，去除不必要的抽象层，并且完全免费和开源，适合各类开发者使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于游戏设计工具的使用场景和技术实现的讨论

不同观点：
• [reedf1] 认为该工具看起来对于软件工程师来说是直观的，并提出疑问该工具的主要使用场景是单人游戏还是多人游戏。这反映了对工具适用范围的关注，尤其是其在不同游戏类型中的应用。

• [kaliqt] 回应并详细介绍了Vircadia的重大技术更新，包括使用PostgreSQL和Bun来提升性能和减少代码膨胀。他们强调这种技术选择在游戏开发中不常见，但在这里却非常有效，能够简化管理并提升开发者体验（DX）。Kaliqt进一步说明该工具的目标是支持更多开发者创建更大规模的世界，并鼓励反馈和原型设计。此外，他们提到未来的路线图包括更多的SDK和进一步减少不必要的功能，以帮助开发者专注于游戏本身而非工具细节。

补充讨论：
• 技术实现的细节：Kaliqt详细解释了使用PostgreSQL和Bun的优势，并提到这些技术选择如何帮助提升性能和可管理性。

• 开发者支持和社区参与：Kaliqt明确表示欢迎开发者提供反馈和分享原型设计，显示出对社区参与的重视。

• 工具的未来发展方向：提到未来的技术发展计划，包括更多SDK的开发和减少不必要的功能，显示出对持续改进和优化开发者体验的承诺。

争议焦点：
• 目前讨论中没有明显的争议，但[reedf1]的提问暗示了对工具定位的某种不确定性，尤其是其在单人游戏和多人游戏开发中的具体应用场景。Kaliqt的回应虽然详细，但未直接明确该工具在单人或多人游戏开发中的偏重。

data.title: North Korean IT Workers Are Being Exposed on a Scale
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 文章主要揭示了一群北韩IT工人在西方公司远程工作，并将收入汇回国内支持金正恩政权。这些工人伪装成合法远程工作者，通过使用假身份或盗用身份 infiltrate 公司，参与从加密货币盗窃到为政权筹集资金的活动。文章特别提到了两名被识别的工人“Naoki Murano”和“Jenson Collins”，他们涉嫌参与了多起网络盗窃，包括从加密货币公司DeltaPrime盗取600万美元。北韩的网络活动复杂且危险，以资助政权、发展武器和收集情报为目标，与传统国家支持的黑客行为不同，更像是一个“国家认可的犯罪集团”。尽管这些工人技术娴熟，但常留下数字痕迹，如照片和网络活动记录，显示他们在奢侈生活中的享乐。文章还提到，这些工人往往自幼被选拔接受专业培训，成为黑客或开发人员。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对标题中删除“massive”一词的动机和性质的讨论

不同观点：
• The-Old-Hacker 的观点：认为删除“massive”可能是某种家长式 censorship（审查），目的是控制或限制编辑在标题中表达情感色彩。这种观点暗示了某种外部干预，可能出于政治或意识形态的原因。
   
• add-sub-mul-div 的观点：质疑“massive”一词的删除是否属于编辑上的调整，或者该词是否一开始就没有出现在网站上。这个观点更倾向于从技术角度解释，认为可能只是编辑过程中的疏漏或更正。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于删除“massive”一词的性质：The-Old-Hacker 认为这是审查，而 add-sub-mul-div 则认为可能是编辑错误或更正。
• 讨论涉及对“编辑色彩”的看法，The-Old-Hacker 认为“massive”增加了情感上的强调，删除它是为了削弱这种色彩，而 add-sub-mul-div 则没有对此作出明确判断，仅对词的存在与否提出质疑。
• 例子方面，The-Old-Hacker 提到了“paternalistic censorship”作为可能的动机，而 add-sub-mul-div 则提出了词可能一开始就不存在作为另一种解释。

The young developers
are having the time of their lives. They pop open bottles of sparkling wine, eat steak dinners, play soccer together, and lounge around in a luxurious private swimming pool, all of their activity captured in photos that were later exposed online. In one picture, a man poses in front of a life-sized
Minions
cardboard cutout. But despite their exuberance, these are not successful Silicon Valley entrepreneurs; they’re
IT workers from the Hermit Kingdom of North Korea
, who infiltrate Western companies and send their wages back home.
Two members of a cluster of North Korean developers, who allegedly operated out of Southeast Asian country Laos before being relocated to Russia by the beginning of 2024, are today being identified by researchers at cybersecurity company
DTEX
. The men, who DTEX believes have used the personas ‘Naoki Murano’ and ‘Jenson Collins,’ are alleged to have been involved in raising money for the brutalist North Korean regime as part of the widespread IT worker epidemic, with Murano alleged to have previously been
linked to a $6 million heist
at crypto firm DeltaPrime last year.
For years, Kim Jong-un’s
North Korea
has posed one of the
most
sophisticated
and
dangerous cyber
threats
to Western countries and businesses, with its hackers stealing the intellectual property needed to develop its own technology, plus looting billions in crypto to evade sanctions and
create nuclear weapons
. In February, the FBI
announced
that North Korea pulled off the biggest ever crypto heist,
stealing $1.5 billion
from crypto exchange Bybit. Alongside its skilled hackers, Pyongyang’s IT workers, who often are based in China or Russia, trick companies into employing them as remote workers and have become an
increasing menace
.
“What we’re doing isn’t working, and if it is working, it’s not working fast enough,” says Michael ‘Barni’ Barnhart, a leading North Korean cyber researcher and principal investigator at DTEX. As well as identifying Murano and Collins, DTEX, in a
detailed report about North Korean cyber activity
, is also
publishing
more than 1,000 email addresses that it alleges to have been identified as linked to North Korean IT worker activity. The move is one of the largest disclosures of North Korean IT worker activity to date.
North Korea’s broad cyber operations can’t be compared with those of other hostile nations, such as Russia and China, Barnhart explains in the DTEX report, as Pyongyang operates like a “state-sanctioned crime syndicate” rather than more traditional military or intelligence operations. Everything is driven by funding the regime, developing weaponry, and gathering information, Barnhart says. “Everything is tied together in some way, shape, or form.”
The Misfits Move In
Around 2022 and 2023, DTEX claims both Naoki Murano and Jenson Collins—their real names are not known—were based in Laos and also travelled between Vladivostok, in Russia. The pair appeared among a wider group of possible North Koreans in Laos, and a cache of their photos were first exposed in an
open Dropbox folder
. The photos were discovered by a collective of North Korean researchers who often collaborate with Barnhart and call themselves a “Misfit” alliance. In recent weeks, they’ve posted
numerous images of purported
North Korean IT workers
online.
North Korea’s IT workers are prolific in their activities, often trying to infiltrate multiple companies simultaneously by using stolen identities or creating false personas to try to appear legitimate. Some use freelance platforms; others try to
recruit international facilitators to run laptop farms
. While their online personas may be fake, the country—where millions do not have basic human rights or
access to the internet
—steers talented children into its education pipeline where they can become skilled developers and hackers. That means many of the IT workers and hackers are likely to know each other, potentially since they were children. Despite being technically adept, they often leave a trail of digital breadcrumbs in their wake.
Murano was first linked to North Korean operations publicly by cryptocurrency investigator
ZachXBT
, who published the names, cryptocurrency wallet details, and email addresses of
more than 20 North Korean IT workers
last year. Murano was then linked to the DeltaPrime heist in
reporting by Coinbase
in October.. Members of the Misfits collective have shared photos of Murano looking
pleased with himself while eating steak
and a picture of an
alleged Japanese passport
.
Meanwhile, Collins, who DTEX included in its report and who was
featured in swimming pool photos
included in the Dropbox folder, was most commonly involved in IT work that generated revenue for Pyongyang, says narcass3 a member of the Misfits who asked to be identified by their online handle. “He seems to have mainly just worked on crypto/blockchain projects, including one which seems to be completely DPR

data.title: Use Method: Linux Performance Checklist
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了使用**USE方法**对Linux系统进行性能检查的详细步骤和命令。USE方法通过分析系统资源的使用率（Utilization）、饱和度（Saturation）和错误（Errors）来发现性能瓶颈和问题。文章列出了针对不同物理资源（如CPU、内存、网络接口、存储设备等）的具体指标和监控命令，帮助系统管理员识别和诊断系统性能问题。文中还提供了用于检查各类资源状态的工具和命令示例，如`vmstat`、`sar`、`free`、`iostat`等，并提到了一些动态追踪工具如DTrace和SystemTap。该方法主要适用于物理系统的命令行环境，但也可部分用于远程监控。

USE Method: Linux Performance Checklist
The
USE Method
provides a strategy for performing a complete check of system health, identifying common bottlenecks and errors.  For each system resource, metrics for utilization, saturation and errors are identified and checked.  Any issues discovered are then investigated using further strategies.
This is an example USE-based metric list for Linux operating systems (eg, Ubuntu, CentOS, Fedora).  This is primarily intended for system administrators of the physical systems, who are using command line tools.  Some of these metrics can be found in remote monitoring tools.

, "us" + "sy" + "st";
sar -u
, sum fields except "%idle" and "%iowait";
dstat -c

mpstat -P ALL 1
, sum fields except "%idle" and "%iowait";

, same as

data.title: Project West Ford
data.author: nabla9
data.article_summary:
**Project West Ford**是美国军方在1961年和1963年进行的一项实验，旨在地球上空创建人工电离层，以解决军事通信的弱点。该项目由麻省理工学院的林肯实验室负责，计划将4.8亿根铜制偶极天线放置在轨道上，形成一个环，以支持全球无线电通信。这些天线长度为1.78厘米，直径分别为25.4微米和17.8微米，设计用于反射8 GHz的信号。

1961年的首次尝试失败，天线未能散开，但1963年的第二次尝试成功实现了通信传输。然而，由于现代通信卫星的发展和国际科学界的抗议，该项目最终被搁置。英国天文学家和皇家天文学会等对实验提出反对，认为其造成了空间碎片。抗议促使1967年的《外层空间条约》增加了协商条款。尽管大部分天线在几年内脱离轨道，但仍有一些未正确散开的天线残留在轨道上，截至2023年4月，仍有44簇天线在轨道上。

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Experimental space-based radio communication project
Needles from the West Ford project compared to a stamp.
Project West Ford
(also known as
Westford Needles
and
Project Needles
) was a test carried out by
Massachusetts Institute of Technology
's
Lincoln Laboratory
on behalf of the
United States military
in 1961 and 1963 to create an artificial
ionosphere
above the Earth.
[
1
]
This was done to solve a major weakness that had been identified in military communications.
[
2
]
History
[
edit
]
At the height of the
Cold War
, all international communications were either sent through
submarine communications cables
or bounced off the natural
ionosphere
. The United States military was concerned that the
Soviets
might cut those cables, forcing the unpredictable ionosphere to be the only means of communication with overseas forces.
[
1
]
To mitigate the potential threat,
Walter E. Morrow
started Project Needles at the MIT Lincoln Laboratory in 1958. The goal of the project was to place a ring of 480,000,000
[
3
]
[
4
]
copper
dipole antennas
in orbit to facilitate global
radio
communication. The dipoles collectively provided passive support to Project West Ford's
parabolic dish
(located at the
Haystack Observatory
in the
town of Westford
) to communicate with distant sites.
The needles used in the experiment were 1.78 centimetres (0.70 in) long and 25.4
micrometres
(1.00
thou
) [1961] or 17.8 micrometres (0.70 thou) [1963] in diameter.
[
5
]
[
6
]
The length was chosen because it was half the
wavelength
of the 8
GHz
signal used in the study.
[
1
]
The needles were placed in
medium Earth orbit
at an altitude of between 3,500 and 3,800 kilometres (2,200–2,400 mi) at inclinations of 96 and 87 degrees.
Westford dipole dispenser exhibit at the
Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center
A first attempt was launched on 21 October 1961,
[
6
]
during which the needles failed to disperse.
[
7
]
[
8
]
The project was eventually successful with the 9 May 1963
[
6
]
launch, with radio transmissions carried by the manufactured ring.
[
9
]
[
8
]
However, the technology was ultimately shelved, partially due to the development of the modern
communications satellite
and partially due to protests from other scientists.
[
1
]
[
2
]
British radio astronomers, optical astronomers, and the
Royal Astronomical Society
protested the experiment.
[
10
]
[
11
]
[
12
]
The Soviet newspaper
Pravda
also joined the protests under the headline "U.S.A. Dirties Space".
[
13
]
The
International Academy of Astronautics
regards the experiment as the worst deliberate release of
space debris
.
[
14
]
At the time, the issue was raised in the
United Nations
where the then United States Ambassador to the United Nations
Adlai Stevenson
defended the project.
[
15
]
Stevenson studied the published journal articles on Project West Ford. Using what he learned on the subject and citing the articles he had read, he successfully allayed the fears of most UN ambassadors from other countries. He and the articles explained that
sunlight pressure
would cause the dipoles to only remain in
orbit
for a short period of approximately three years. The international protest ultimately resulted in a consultation provision included in the 1967
Outer Space Treaty
.
[
1
]
[
10
]
Although the dispersed needles in the second experiment removed themselves from orbit within a few years,
[
4
]
some of the dipoles that had not deployed correctly remained in clumps, contributing a small amount of the orbital debris tracked by
NASA's Orbital Debris Program Office
.
[
16
]
[
17
]
Their numbers have been diminishing over time as they occasionally re-enter.  As of April 2023
[update]
, 44 clumps of needles larger than 10 cm were still known to be in orbit.

data.title: The cryptography behind passkeys
data.author: tatersolid
data.article_summary:
这篇文章简要介绍了密码学中的身份验证，特别是通过加密技术实现的更安全的用户认证方式——** passkeys（通行密钥）**。虽然加密通常让人想到加密保密，但身份验证同样重要。传统的密码容易受到钓鱼攻击和数据泄露的威胁，而passkeys通过加密技术提供更强的安全性。

**Passkey的加密基础**是基于公私钥对的数字签名。注册时，网站保存公钥和标识符；验证时，网站提供挑战并等待包含该挑战的签名响应。由于服务器仅保存公钥，且用户不发送敏感信息，即使服务器被黑客攻击也不会泄露敏感数据。

然而，**WebAuthn** 规范通过绑定来源（origin binding）解决了钓鱼问题。浏览器将请求的来源传递给认证器，认证器只在请求来源与创建passkey的网站匹配时使用密钥对，从而防止钓鱼攻击。此外，WebAuthn只允许使用HTTPS的来源，确保请求来自具有有效证书的服务器。

**认证器类型**包括硬件或软件，可以验证用户的存在，某些还可以结合“用户所知”进行多因素认证。

总结来说，passkeys通过加密技术及WebAuthn规范实现了一种防钓鱼的强身份验证机制。

主要讨论点： passkeys技术的优缺点、同步与安全性问题、以及与现有身份验证方法的比较

不同观点：
• labadal：喜欢passkeys的生物认证功能，但担心厂商锁定问题，关注标准化的进展。
• lxgr：提到一种基于密码短语的身份验证方法，但提醒这种方法类似于“脑钱包”，存在安全隐患，不建议用于重要场合。同时分享了一个自己实现的项目来展示技术可行性。
• whartung：质疑在不同设备和操作系统之间切换时，passkeys的有效性和密码恢复能力。
• petedoyle：关注passkey同步背后的加密强度，尤其是基于4-6位数字锁码的加密是否容易被暴力破解，担心实际熵值不足。
• nemoniac：质疑浏览器在passkeys流程中的必要性。
• joelthelion：询问passkeys是否正在获得实际应用。
• throw7：希望有一种平台身份验证器可以导入/导出明文的密钥对和凭证ID，以避免厂商锁定和云备份，提到目前使用TOTP的方案更为灵活。
• solarkraft：认为挑战-响应结合非对称加密的身份验证方式（如SSH）更为理想，批评passkeys缺乏备份和互操作性，并分享了一次失败的创建经历。
• andrewmcwatters：认为现有密码和密码管理器已经足够好，TOTP广泛支持，质疑passkeys的实际需求和可移植性，批评大公司推动的技术锁定。

补充讨论：
• 关于passkeys同步的安全性：peteodoyle对同步过程中使用的锁码强度和实际熵值表示担忧，认为可能存在被暴力破解的风险。
• 关于passkeys的互操作性和备份问题：多个评论者（throw7, solarkraft, andrewmcwatters）提到passkeys在不同设备间的互操作性差，缺乏有效的备份和导入/导出机制，导致厂商锁定问题。
• 关于passkeys的实际应用和接受度：joelthelion和andrewmcwatters质疑passkeys是否正在获得实际应用和用户接受，认为现有方案已经能满足大部分需求。

争议焦点：
• passkeys的厂商锁定问题和缺乏可移植性是主要争议点，多个评论者对此表示不满，并与TOTP等现有方案进行对比，认为后者更为灵活。
• passkeys的安全性和备份机制也是争议的焦点，尤其是同步过程中的加密强度和实际应用中的可靠性。

43983159.article_content:
When most people think of cryptography, the first thing they typically think of is encryption: keeping information confidential. But just as important (if not more) is authenticity: ensuring that information is really coming from an authentic source. When you visit a website, the server typically proves its identity through a Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate authenticated by the Web Public Key Infrastructure (PKI). Passwords are the traditional solution for user authentication, but they suffer from phishing attacks and data breaches. This is where passkeys come in.
Instead of explaining what passkeys are and why they are better than passwords—
something
many
other
resources
have already covered—this post will examine the cryptography behind passkeys, the guarantees they do or do not give, and interesting cryptographic things you can do with them, such as generating cryptographic keys and storing certificates. You need to understand the cryptography behind passkeys to implement secure authentication correctly. We’ll also discuss the main passkey specification, WebAuthn, and show you how to use extensions of passkey mechanisms to build a more intricate system with different capabilities.
Passkey cryptography basics
At their core, passkeys are just key pairs used to produce digital signatures. When registering a passkey, the website saves the public key and an identifier. When authenticating a user via a passkey, the website provides a challenge and waits for a signed response including this challenge (and some other metadata, such as the identifier). The identifier is used to look up the public key, which is used to verify the signature.
From a cryptographic perspective, this is quite straightforward. The private key authenticates the user, but no sensitive information useful to an attacker is communicated to the server. If the server challenge is properly generated—e.g., as a uniformly random sequence of 32 bytes—then it will prevent replay attacks. Since the server holds only a public key and the user does not send it sensitive information, there is nothing to be leaked in case of a hack.
But digital signatures alone aren’t enough to solve the phishing problem. If we stopped here with just the cryptographic primitives, users would still be vulnerable. For instance, without additional safeguards, an attacker might trick users into signing challenges for the wrong website or reusing the same key pair across multiple sites.
This is why passkeys are built on the
W3C’s WebAuthn
specification, which adds crucial security properties beyond the basic cryptography. Let’s look at how WebAuthn transforms these simple cryptographic primitives into a phishing-resistant authentication system.
WebAuthn
WebAuthn is the main specification behind passkeys. In simple terms, users access a
website
(relying party) through their
browser
(WebAuthn user agent) on a
device
such as a laptop, phone, or PC (client device). The browser interacts with an
authenticator
, a piece of hardware or software that generates the passkey key pair, and creates digital signatures using this key pair.
Figure 1: Simplified view of a passkey authentication flow.
In the diagram above, you can see how a passkey authentication works:
The website requests authentication through the browser.
The browser communicates with the authenticator.
The authenticator checks credentials and user presence.
The authenticator returns a signed response.
The browser forwards this response to the website for verification.
(This interaction between browser and authenticator is described in more detail in another specification: the FIDO Alliance’s
Client to Authenticator Protocol
(CTAP).) This is a simplified description; the WebAuthn specification allows for a larger variety of use cases (e.g., everything could work via a mobile application instead of a website/browser). However, those specifics are not relevant to understanding how passkeys work with cryptography.
Anti-phishing protections
WebAuthn solves the phishing problem through origin binding. The specification requires browsers to provide the
origin
of the request (i.e., the website domain) to the authenticator. The authenticator in turn uses passkeys only when the website making the request matches the website that created the passkey.
This means that if you create a passkey for bank.com, a phishing site at fake-bank.com simply cannot use it—your authenticator will refuse the request. Each website also gets its own unique key pair, eliminating the password reuse problem entirely.
Additionally, the specification allows only origins that use HTTPS, which means that the request comes from a server that has a valid certificate for the corresponding origin.
Types of authenticators
Generally, authenticators are “something you have.” All authenticators can check whether a user is actually present when authenticating. Some authenticators can additionally verify the user according to “something they know,” such as

  - [gyomu] 认为HDR内容在社交媒体上的显示效果过于刺眼，尤其是在夜间或低亮度环境下使用时，体验较差。相比之下，全屏HDR内容（如游戏和电影）则表现较好。
  - [CarVac] 同样认为当前的HDR显示不舒服，尤其是当亮度过高时，如室内照片中的白墙被显示得过于明亮。

• **HDR技术实现与色彩管理问题**：  
  - [mxfh] 批评文章未深入讨论消费级数字环境下的色彩管理问题，并指出用户界面在HDR下未经过充分测试，可能导致字幕等内容过于刺眼。同时提到Dolby Vision和Apple在封闭平台上的领先地位，而开放网络环境中的HDR仍不成熟。
  - [the__alchemist] 认为HDR技术的潜在价值毋庸置疑，可以显著提升视觉体验，但过去由于市场未成熟，HDR显示器未普及，如今可能值得重新考虑购买。

• **技术细节与实现方法的争议**：  
  - [sergioisidoro] 提到在模拟摄影中，通过显影剂的补偿作用可以达到更高的动态范围，而不仅仅是通过遮挡和燃烧技术。同时批评手机上的HDR功能虽然适合记录家庭时刻，但不适合作为创意工具。
  - [tomatotomato37] 提供了更多技术资料链接，建议对HDR技术感兴趣的读者深入了解。

• **浏览器兼容性问题**：  
  - [echo_time] 指出在Firefox浏览器上查看相关内容时遇到困惑，而在Chrome浏览器上则体验更好，怀疑Firefox缺少某些设置。
  - [sebstefan] 提到在Firefox的画中画模式下，某些设计问题得以解决，但文章中的特定演示未触发画中画选项。

• **HDR技术的市场接受度与技术门槛**：  
  - [aidenn0] 指出HDR和4K显示的普及面临巨大的基础设施升级成本，消费者可能需要很长时间才能完全接受这些新技术。
  - [bookofjoe] 代表普通用户表示对技术细节不感兴趣，只希望设备开箱即用，不愿意手动调整各种设置。

• **HDR技术的支持与期待**：  
  - [randall] 表示对文章和HDR效果的赞赏，特别是HDR照片展示令他印象深刻。
  - [c-fe] 虽然对当前的HDR内容持怀疑态度，但期待某些摄影应用（如Halide）能带来更好的HDR体验。

补充讨论：
• **HDR与亮度的关系**：  
  - [perching_aix] 提到显示器的亮度输出与自然光不同，即便自然光亮度更高，显示器上的高亮内容仍可能刺眼。同时指出HDR与高亮度是两个不同的概念，HDR只是一种表示方式，高亮度并非HDR的必要条件。

• **相机动态范围问题**：  
  - [fogleman] 质疑文章未解释清楚相机在动态范围不足的情况下如何通过单次曝光实现HDR效果。

争议焦点：
• HDR技术的实际用户体验与技术实现之间的矛盾，尤其是在非全屏应用（如日常计算和网页浏览）中，HDR显示的舒适性和色彩管理问题。

data.title: How the economics of multitenancy work
data.author: tsaifu
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Blacksmith如何通过多租户经济模式实现盈利，特别是在处理CI（持续集成）工作负载方面的独特优势。CI工作负载具有高度不稳定和短暂的特性，通常在工作时间出现高峰，而非全天候运行。这种不规则性使得传统硬件管理变得不切实际，而Blacksmith的serverless CI云平台则通过资源池化和按需计费，解决了这一问题。

Blacksmith使用数百台裸金属游戏CPU，通过Firecracker技术在需求出现时快速启动微虚拟机，任务完成后立即销毁。由于这些硬件成本是固定的，Blacksmith的关键在于提高利用率。通过吸引多个客户，他们能够平滑高峰需求，将原本的资源浪费转化为持续的收入。随着客户数量增加，CI任务的随机性逐渐形成一个可预测的模式，从而最大化资源利用率和利润。这种模式不仅为客户提供了灵活性，也确保了Blacksmith的可持续盈利。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CI/CD管道中的资源分配与多租户架构的效率和成本优化

不同观点：
• **动态CPU分配支持者**（zdc1）：建议采用动态CPU分配或类似Jenkin's flyweight runner的概念，以解决像CloudFormation等管道在等待完成时长时间占用零CPU但仍按固定资源收费的问题。这种方法可以在低使用率时提高资源利用率，甚至可以通过超额销售实现200%的利用率。

• **动态资源分配的质疑者**（mgaunard）：认为动态扩展不仅不会显著降低成本，反而可能导致系统变慢。由于无法预先知道CI所需的资源，动态资源分配存在困难。

• **混合资源使用建议者**（coolcase）：提出将多个服务整合到Kubernetes集群等技术中，以平滑资源使用高峰，减少浪费和不必要的扩展。这种方法在云环境中特别有效，可以帮助利用保留实例和折扣来降低成本。

• **固定基础与峰值使用结合的建议者**（Havoc）：认为固定基础加上用于峰值的spot定价VM组合可能更具成本效益，而不是当前的固定租赁模式。

• **多租户与时间共享的类比者**（TuringTest）：将当前讨论的多租户概念与旧时代的主机“时间共享”相比较，认为这是旧概念的新应用。

• **成本与使用量关系的分析者**（mlhpdx）：指出多租户SaaS公司希望成本是使用量的次线性函数，而这种大容量单元除以小工作单元的模式是实现这一目标的一种方式。不过在低量时，这种方法是阶梯式的，只有在大量时才变得线性，因此只在增长阶段具有显著效果。

• **服务器无延迟问题的提出者**（shadowgovt）：关注服务器无延迟问题，指出某些无服务器系统在处理峰值时可能引入前置延迟。尽管在长时间运行的CI过程中，这种延迟可能不重要，但在紧密开发循环中却是痛苦的。不过，如果峰值是规律的，足够先进的无服务器系统可以提前准备计算资源以应对峰值。

• **多租户的非计算效率支持者**（0xbadcafebee）：认为多租户的经济效益不仅仅在于高效计算，还在于其他效率，如人力成本、组织成本和功能效率。

补充讨论：
- 动态资源分配与固定资源分配的成本与效率对比。
- 多租户架构在不同业务场景中的应用与效益分析。
- 服务器无延迟问题在CI/CD管道中的重要性与解决方案探讨。
